name: Kalshi
positioning: CFTC-regulated US event-contract exchange positioning itself as "the market for everything" (brand-kit sample copy) / "Prediction Market for Trading the Future" (homepage title). Institutional-brokerage credibility fused with a pop-culture, sports-first growth engine: App Store name is currently "Kalshi: Trade the World Cup" (subtitle "FIFA World Cup 2026"), claiming 10M+ users and "largest legal and federally regulated prediction market" while the marketing voice runs campaigns like "MAKE MONEY ON DRAMA." Product breadth: event contracts across 12 categories, plus Perps (perpetual futures, top-level nav), Combos (multi-leg parlays), an API for algo traders, and 3.25% interest on cash balances advertised inside the trade ticket. Regulation is used as an offensive differentiator vs Polymarket/sportsbooks — a top-level TRUST nav menu, "Markets over Monopolies" advocacy page, and footer line "Kalshi is subject to U.S. regulatory oversight by the CFTC" — even as it fights state gaming regulators in court.
visualLanguage: Near-black UI (#0A0C10-ish) with mint/emerald green as the single hero color. Brand kit (fetched) specifies: Primary Green 1 #00DD94, Primary Green 2 #00CE8E, Light Green #CEFFEF, Dark Green #01201A; secondary palette (Blue #079CFF, Violet #8F5BFF, Red #FF0026, Orange #FF770F, Navy #002070, Purple #3E008A, Burgundy #500010, Dark Red #990F02) explicitly subordinate to green. Background-only gradients in three sanctioned ramps (Light→Primary, Primary→Dark, Dark→Black). Semantic color is strict: green = positive/Yes/price-up, red = negative/No/price-down/LIVE dot. Live sports cards get a subtle red-tinted border glow; the Combo button uses a violet gradient border. A "Rivalry Match" module system builds head-to-head visuals on Kalshi Dark Green with dual team-color gradients (80%→0% opacity). Probability pills are thin green-outlined capsules; price-history charts are line charts on dark with a "Kalshi" watermark and live money-flow annotations ("+$408") floating on the chart. Category avatar/sub-brand lockup system (Politics, Crypto, Culture, Climate, Sports, Research) for navigation and social. Playful mascot illustration appears on the 404 (robot reading a hole-riddled newspaper) — the seriousness is in the data surfaces, not the brand's tone.
typographyBrand: Fully custom, publicly documented type system (kalshi.com/brandkit, fetched live): "Kalshi Sans" — a geometric sans hybridized with European-grotesk architecture — for body/UI; "Kalshi Sans Condensed" for headlines and large display ("Fast, tall, unmistakably Kalshi"); "XCondensed" reserved for product headlines and social; and a dot-matrix data face, "OO Theran" (always Light weight), for tickers/live numbers with green=positive/red=negative encoding. Five weights per family (Light→Bold); prescribed weight-pairing formulas (consecutive vs skipped weights) instead of size jumps. Casing rules: UPPERCASE only for breaking-news/high-impact moments, Title/Sentence case for neutral editorial tone. In the live product: condensed display face for market titles ("Conor McGregor vs Max Holloway", "Browse Markets"), letter-spaced all-caps micro-labels for nav/breadcrumbs (SPORTS · MMA · MCGREGOR VS. HOLLOWAY 2), tabular numerals everywhere for prices/percentages. Green wordmark with codified clear space (K-stem width), 72px digital minimum, and an unusually strict misuse section.
navigationDiscovery: Desktop: top bar = wordmark, MARKETS (/browse), PERPS (/perps), LIVE with red live-event counter badge ("LIVE 42", ticked up to 45 during the session) (/calendar), SOCIAL (/ideas/feed), TRUST (dropdown to six policy-center pages + mission), global search with placeholder "Trade on anything", Log in / green Sign up pill. Second row = persistent category rail: Trending, Elections, Politics, Sports, Culture, Crypto, Commodities, Climate, Economics, Mentions, Finance, Tech & Science (each → /category/*). Homepage is editorially curated: a hero carousel ("1 of 7") featuring a live market with real-time chart plus a one-sentence "News" context blurb; right rail with mega-event tiles showing lifetime volume ("FIFA World Cup — $11,337,736,058 total volume", "2026 US Elections — $483,510,415"), and a Trending list (market + leading outcome + % + day delta). /browse adds sort/filter pills (Trending ▾, Frequency ▾, All categories ▾) over a 3-column card grid. Market pages cross-sell via "Game Props" sub-market tabs (Method of Victory, Round of Finish...), "People are also trading", "New Markets", "Related Markets", "Related Topics". Social sidebar has a "Request market" button — user-sourced market ideas. Footer holds Product/Company/Help link stacks incl. Fee schedule, Trading hours, Regulatory, Brand Kit. Note: guessable URL /markets 404s (real path is /browse).
marketCardAnatomy: Browse/home card (observed at 1280px): (1) header row — small event thumbnail + ALL-CAPS category label (SOCCER, MMA, BASEBALL) left, series context right ("FIFA World Cup", "Pro Baseball", "ITF"); (2) event title in display face ("Norway vs England: Goalscorer"); (3) status line — red-dot LIVE badge with in-game state ("2nd - 47'", "▼7TH", set scores for tennis) or start time ("Jul 12 @ 4:20AM"); (4) up to two outcome rows: outcome name underlined in its team/outcome color, payout multiplier in muted text ("2.34x", "12.5x"), and a green-outlined percent pill ("41%"); live game cards embed actual scores in small boxes inline with each team row; (5) footer row — dollar volume left ("$88,721,707 vol"), links right ("Spread and Total", "34 markets" count for the full event). Market detail page adds: breadcrumb, countdown ("Begins in 4h 9m 01s"), price-history chart (0–100% axis, 1D/1W/1M/ALL toggles, live trade-amount annotations), an outcome table with "Chance" column (28% ▼3) and per-row Yes/No price buttons ("Yes 28¢ / No 73¢"), visible exchange tickers (Series KXUFCFIGHT / Event / Market), "Timeline and payout" module (open date, close trigger, "Projected payout: 5 minutes after closing"), plain-language Market Rules with named verification sources, and an embedded social activity feed.
tradeTicketClarity: Right-rail ticket (desktop, logged-out): Buy/Sell tabs; denomination dropdown defaulting to DOLLARS (dollar-first sizing rather than contract counts — beginner-friendly; dropdown implies a contracts mode); selected outcome name; YES 73¢ / NO 28¢ segmented toggle with live prices; a "3.25% Interest" note on cash; $ amount input; live-computed "Odds" row translating to "74% chance" (with info icon) and "Max payout" with dollar figure and settlement date ("Jul 26, 2026"); big green CTA ("Sign up to trade"). A gradient-bordered COMBO button above the ticket opens a parlay builder (/combos/ufc/ufc). On mobile, outcome rows collapse to full-width paired "Yes 28¢ / No 73¢" buttons. Fees are NOT itemized in the ticket by default: help center says per-market fees sit behind an "i" info icon, with the canonical source a PDF (kalshi.com/docs/kalshi-fee-schedule.pdf, updated 7.7.26). Per third-party summaries of that schedule: taker fee ≈ round(0.07 × price × (1−price)) per contract for most categories (max ~1.75¢ at 50¢), premium multipliers on some categories (e.g., crypto), maker fee = 25% of taker on maker-fee markets, no settlement/membership/ACH deposit/withdrawal fees. Sports data (scores, clock) is integrated directly into the ticket context for live trading.
trustRiskSafety: The deepest trust stack in the category, woven into primary navigation: TRUST top-nav menu → policy-center pages for Trust & Safety for Families, Stopping insider trading, Responsible trading tools, Banned markets, Market integrity, Markets over Monopolies; homepage carries a three-card trust strip ("Market integrity — Learn how we keep markets fair", "Markets over Monopolies — Fair markets protect consumers", "Responsible trading — Tools and tips for trading smart"). Every market page shows: plain-language resolution rule ("Resolves Yes if Max Holloway wins..."), named outcome-verification sources ("Outcome verified from The Wall Street Journal, ESPN, and Fox Sports"), an "Important information" edge-case callout (draw/no-contest → 50/50, cancellation → fair-price, post-expiration reversals ignored), "View full rules" + Help center links, a full insider-trading prohibition list (players, coaches, staff, owners, source-agency employees, MNPI holders, household members) with a "Report Insider Trading" link, IP non-endorsement disclaimer, and exchange ticker codes. Rulebook is public (kalshi.com/regulatory/rulebook); disputes go to an Outcome Review Committee, with Rule 6.3(c) allowing settlement at last price if unresolvable. Responsible-trading hub lists six numbered tools — trading breaks, self-exclusion (plus ecosystem-wide SelfExclude.io via IC360), monthly deposit limits, Birches Health mental-health partnership, education, 2FA — with step-by-step paths to the in-product "Responsible Risk Management" settings; funds NCPG initiative; 988 lifeline listed; an AI "Health Check" tool was announced in press. Footer: full risk disclaimer + CFTC oversight statement; 18+ App Store rating. Counterweights: NCPG says tools fall short of licensed-sportsbook standards (no mandatory loss alerts, no standardized screening); fee transparency lives in a PDF; and legality is contested — 2025-26 state actions (Massachusetts injunction, Ohio federal loss, Arizona criminal charges, NY class action) vs federal wins (Third Circuit affirmed preliminary injunction Apr 6 2026; CFTC/DOJ sued three states Apr 2 2026).
socialCommunity: Kalshi Social launched as a first-class surface (SOCIAL in top nav → /ideas/feed; dedicated mobile tab). Observed: left rail (Feed, Your Profile, Leaderboard, white "Make a post" pill, "Request market"); composer with "What's on your mind?", GIF support, and "+ Add a position" — posts embed verified bet-slip cards (green gradient receipt: market, "Target Price: $64,317.48 / Yes", COST $61.58 / PAID OUT $92.37); time-scope pills (Now/Today/This Week/This Month); like/comment/bookmark/share actions. Market pages embed a live Activity feed ("This event | All") where most posts are position shares (including multi-leg combos) with short captions and replies. Per Kalshi's own announcements (Jan 2026 X posts) and help center: personalized For You feed, follow-with-trade-alerts ("get notified the moment they move"), "Inner Circle" private groups for sharing trades, Live Chat during events, every user gets a public Social profile by default (editable), profiles expose open/closed positions and trade history, leaderboard participation is opt-out-by-default (users are auto-opted OUT per help center), community guidelines plus report/block tooling. Third-party scrapers already harvest profiles/leaderboards. Signal quality is low in raw feeds (one-word captions, slip-dumps) — ranking, not volume, is the open problem.
mobileUsability: Mobile web (observed at 375×812): simplified header (wordmark + Log in/Sign up), horizontally scrollable category rail, breadcrumbs truncate with ellipsis, display-type titles wrap gracefully, outcome rows stack with full-width Yes/No price buttons, and a native-feeling bottom tab bar — Browse, Live (with red live-event count), Search, Social. Native apps: iOS 4.8★ (354K ratings, fetched from listing; earlier reviews cite 4.7★/22K) and Android ~4.5★/3K+; app is ~265MB, requires iOS 15+, 18+ rated; recent release notes are generic ("Bug fixes and performance upgrades") with frequent releases (v9.9.94 two days before fetch). Reviewers praise near-parity with desktop (hamburger menu, search bar, market thumbnails, few-tap trading) but consistently flag the KYC wall before product exploration, an exchange-like density that intimidates mainstream users, occasional crashes and info-density complaints in recent App Store reviews, and fee grumbling. Site is desktop-first in information hierarchy (third-party assessment) and technically heavy: in our headless session the SPA showed blank-frame flashes and virtualization artifacts during scroll, and kalshi.com aggressively rate-limits non-browser fetchers (HTTP 429).
learnFrom: Make trust a navigation destination, not a footer: a TRUST menu linking to plain-English policy pages (market integrity, insider trading, responsible trading, banned markets) plus a homepage trust-card strip.

Put resolution provenance on every market: one-sentence plain-language rule ('Resolves Yes if...'), NAMED verification sources (WSJ/ESPN/Fox Sports), an edge-case 'Important information' callout, and a 'Timeline and payout' module stating exactly when money moves ('Projected payout: 5 minutes after closing').

Expose exchange-grade artifacts as trust theater that costs nothing: visible series/event/market ticker codes, public rulebook link, insider-trading prohibition list with a report link on the market page itself.

Dollar-first trade ticket with live translation math: amount in → 'Odds: 74% chance' + 'Max payout: $X' recomputed live, with Buy/Sell tabs and a denomination toggle for pros — novice-safe without dumbing down.
Dual probability language: % chance pills for the news-brain, payout multipliers (2.34x) for the betting-brain, cents pricing for the trader-brain — same number, three renderings, chosen per surface.
Live-state market cards: red-dot LIVE + game clock/score embedded in outcome rows, red border glow for live events, countdown timers pre-event — cards feel like scoreboard tiles, not static lists.

Editorial curation layers: hero carousel pairing a market with a one-line 'News' context sentence; Trending rail with outcome + delta; mega-event tiles wearing lifetime volume as social proof; 'Request market' for user-sourced supply.

Skin-in-the-game social: posts embed verified position receipts (cost vs payout), follow-a-trader alerts, private Inner Circles, leaderboard opt-OUT default plus report/block — social proof grounded in real trades, not talk.

A codified data-display type voice: dedicated numeric/ticker face with strict green=up/red=down semantics, tabular figures, and condensed display face for market titles — makes probability feel like a live instrument.

Numbered, findable safety tools: responsible-trading page lists six tools with exact in-app navigation steps ('Settings → Responsible Risk Management'), ecosystem-wide self-exclusion (SelfExclude.io), and third-party health partners with hotlines.
Monetize idle balances into trust: advertising interest on cash (3.25%) inside the ticket reframes 'deposit' as 'brokerage account', not 'gambling wallet'.
Sub-brand avatar system per category (Politics/Sports/Culture...) that keeps one master brand while giving each vertical a recognizable social identity.
avoid: Fee opacity: no dollar fee line in the default ticket — fees hide behind an info icon and a canonical PDF. Show the effective fee inline before confirmation; reviewers and users consistently complain about 'surprise' fees.

KYC wall before value: forcing signup/verification before letting users explore markets is the most-cited onboarding friction in reviews; an auto-popping 'Create your account' modal on first homepage visit compounds it.

SPA heaviness and anti-bot aggression: kalshi.com 429s ordinary fetchers, and the virtualized feed black-flashes on scroll in constrained renderers — costs SEO, shareability, accessibility, and low-end mobile performance.
Broken guessable routes: /markets (the obvious URL, and the nav label) 404s because the real route is /browse — nav labels and URLs should agree.

Categorical legality claims while jurisdiction is contested: 'largest legal and federally regulated' marketing invites the Massachusetts/Ohio/Arizona-style backlash; a young platform should under-claim and let structure prove trust.
Renaming the app around each event cycle ('Kalshi: Trade the World Cup'): boosts event SEO but churns brand recognition and looks promotional in a category needing stability signals.
Unranked social feeds: the raw market-page feed is position-dumps with one-word captions — volume without curation reads as noise/degeneracy and undermines the institutional aesthetic.

Default-public trading profiles: every user gets a Social profile by default with open/closed positions exposed (scrapers already harvest them); privacy defaults for financial activity should be conservative.

Desktop-first density as the only mode: order books and data density serve intentful traders but reviewers call the aesthetic intimidating; a mainstream-facing product needs a progressive-disclosure simple mode.

Safety tools that are voluntary-only: NCPG specifically flags absence of mandatory loss alerts and standardized screening vs sportsbook norms — matching Kalshi here is matching the floor, not the bar.

INFERENCE: DOLLARS dropdown implies a contracts/advanced mode (not toggled while logged out); fee display 'behind info icon' inferred from help-center description of a GIF I could not view; 'desktop-first hierarchy' and 'steep learning curve' are third-party reviewer judgments I partially corroborated; virtualization/perf critique inferred from headless-render behavior which may not reflect real-device performance. ASSUMPTION: logged-in flows (order confirmation screen, actual fee line at confirm, limit-order UI, KYC steps, Responsible Risk Management settings screen) were not observable without an account — descriptions of those rely on help-center text and reviews. No trades were executed and no account was created during research.
